reasoning: The core question — does the difference-in-means refusal direction survive quantization (FP16 -> 8-bit -> 4-bit) — is directly and quantitatively answered by Chhabra & Khalili (arXiv 2504.04215, "Towards Understanding and Improving Refusal in Compressed Models via Mechanistic Interpretability"), which extracts refusal directions under INT8 (LLM.int8()) and 4-bit (NF4) quantization and reports cross-precision cosine similarities of 0.991-0.997 with only ~4% correlation degradation, finding that quantization (unlike pruning) preserves the refusal direction and refusal behavior. The proposal's headline finding is therefore already established: the safety signal survives quantization. The one element not exactly covered is part (b), re-evaluating a separately-trained linear detection probe's AUROC at each precision; the cited work measures the direction and refusal behavior rather than a probe's AUROC, leaving only a minor, incremental gap. Given the problem is substantively solved and the proposed method (difference-in-means, cosine similarity across precisions, small open model on one GPU) closely mirrors the existing paper's method, this is largely addressed rather than partially.

evidence.title: Towards Understanding and Improving Refusal in Compressed Models via Mechanistic Interpretability (Chhabra & Khalili, 2025)
evidence.summary: Directly studies the refusal direction in quantized models (INT8 via LLM.int8(), 4-bit NF4). Reports cosine similarity of refusal directions across precisions of 0.991-0.997 and only ~4% correlation degradation under INT8/INT4, concluding quantization preserves the refusal direction and refusal behavior (whereas pruning shifts it). Uses the same difference-in-means extraction the proposal proposes, and proposes AIRD to recover residual safety loss. This addresses the proposal's headline question (measure (a) cosine similarity across precisions).

evidence.title: Investigating the Impact of Quantization Methods on the Safety and Reliability of LLMs (arXiv 2502.15799)
evidence.summary: Studies how PTQ methods affect LLM safety/refusal behavior, showing quantization can silently weaken safety guardrails. Establishes that the broader problem of quantization's effect on the safety signal is an active, populated research area.

evidence.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction (Arditi et al., 2024)
evidence.summary: The originating work establishing the difference-in-means refusal direction the proposal builds on. The detection-probe and direction-extraction tooling proposed is standard and well-established, not novel.

evidence.title: Exploiting LLM Quantization (arXiv 2405.18137)
evidence.summary: Demonstrates quantization-induced safety changes (vulnerabilities dormant at full precision exposed after 4-bit quantization), reinforcing that the interaction between quantization and the safety signal is already a studied phenomenon.

evidence.title: How Quantization Impacts Privacy Risk on LLMs for Code (arXiv 2508.00128)
evidence.summary: Reports 4-bit quantization degrading membership-inference probe ROC_AUC by up to ~10%, showing prior work has already measured probe AUROC degradation under 4-bit quantization for a safety-relevant signal — analogous to the proposal's part (b).
